_: Shared behavioural table for the SCENARIO refusals — see scripts/check-mirrors.js check 17. `jayhind-client-back/src/const/scenario.const.ts` enforces them; `jayhindi-client-front/src/utils/scenario-rules.util.ts` states them on the scenarios master screen and on the voucher entry surface, so an operator reads the reason instead of meeting a 400 on a control that looked live. Both must answer every expanded row with the SAME SENTENCE, and both must match the sentence stated here — so a wording one side quietly improved, and a rule both sides forgot together, are different failures.
__notMirrored: ⚠️ Only the REFUSALS are mirrored, never `scenarioSql`. The predicate deciding which entries a report may see is server-side alone: the browser never re-derives a figure — every statement renders what came back — so a copy would be a rule with NO READER, which P8b-2 shipped (a `varianceVerdict` copy nothing called) and whose own UI gate proved by injecting a wrong verdict there and passing 6/6. A mirror exists so a screen does not OFFER what the server will refuse; a SQL fragment is not an offer. Checks 15 and 16 carry the same note one master over.
__oneArmHasNoBrowserCopyAtAll: ⚠️⚠️ `describeScenarioMoveBlock` — may a POSTED entry be moved in or out of a scenario? — is deliberately NOT in the client file and is not compared here. It is not a refusal any screen can make: nothing in the SPA edits `journal_entries.scenarioId`, and the one path that changes a posted voucher's scenario (editing an approved Journal) does it by REVERSING and superseding, which is what that rule prescribes rather than what it forbids. Mirroring it would be P8b-2's reader-less copy a second time. It is asserted by `scenario.const.spec.ts` and by `qa:p8e-scenarios` instead.
__bothArmsAreTheBrowsers: ⚠️ Unlike check 16, NEITHER mirrored arm is passed a `null` placeholder. `entryCount` is on the row `GET /scenarios` already returns — the list exists to answer "what would including this do?" before a report is run — and the voucher kind is the segment the entry screen is routed on. So both refusals are made in the browser with no request leaving the page, and the UI gate counts requests rather than reading the sentence alone (a 400 caught and toasted looks identical on screen).
__theKindSetIsDataToo: The two kinds are compared as DATA as well as in the sentence: a side that offered the scenario field on a third kind would disagree about the SET rather than merely about the wording, and the entry surface reads `SCENARIO_VOUCHER_KINDS` to decide whether to render the control at all.

messages.need-name: A scenario needs a name — it is what a report says it is showing.
messages.name-too-long: A scenario name is at most 120 characters.
messages.bad-kind: "${kind}" is not a scenario kind — a voucher is either optional or provisional.
messages.delete-holding-one: "${name}" holds 1 entry that are deliberately out of the books. It can be made inactive, not erased — deleting it would leave those entries in no scenario and still out of the accounts, which is neither.
messages.delete-holding-many: "${name}" holds ${entryCount} entries that are deliberately out of the books. It can be made inactive, not erased — deleting it would leave those entries in no scenario and still out of the accounts, which is neither.
messages.voucher-settles: A payment or receipt cannot be put in a scenario — approving it settles real bills and moves what a document still owes, and money that is out of the accounts cannot close an invoice that is in them. Model it as a Journal instead.
messages.voucher-stock: Only a Journal or a Contra can be put in a scenario. Approving this voucher also moves stock and puts it on a GST return, and neither of those reads the scenario — so it would be out of the accounts and in the books at the same time.

scenario.why: Well-formed. `kind: null` is the omitted field — the DTO leaves it out and the COLUMN carries the default, because an initialiser on the DTO would be a value the pipe supplies on every request including a PUT (§12, BUG-0020).

⚠️ The whitespace-only row is what exercises the TRIM, and both sides have to do it in the same place: the dialog judges the trimmed value because the server stores the trimmed value, or the browser accepts "   " and the save that follows refuses it.
121 characters — the column is `varchar(120)`, so the sentence is what stops MySQL truncating a report header silently or answering with a raw data-too-long error (API-023's family).

⚠️ `OPTIONAL` is here on purpose: the enum is lower-case and a case-insensitive match would store a value the column's own ENUM refuses, turning a readable sentence into a database error. `true` is what a checkbox sends when somebody re-types the field as a boolean.

delete.why: Nothing filed under it, so there is nothing to preserve — and since BUG-0073 the delete that follows is HARD, because a tombstone would cost the name for ever under `UNIQUE(companyId, name)`. `null` is the absent count, which must read as zero rather than as unknown: the list always carries the figure.
⚠️ The singular, because these sentences COUNT things. It is a separate vector rather than an interpolation of the plural so the table states the exact string a reader sees.

⚠️ It ARCHIVES rather than erasing, and the reason is unusual enough that the sentence has to carry it: not that the rows are evidence, but that erasing the scenario would change what the SURVIVING rows mean — an entry whose `scenarioId` points at nothing is excluded by the default and included by no scenario, so it is invisible to every report AND in none of them.

voucher.why: ⚠️ **No scenario is no question.** The rule is asked at both write seams on EVERY save, including the overwhelming majority that carry nothing — so an absent id has to be silent on every kind, or a sales invoice could not be saved at all.

The two kinds whose ENTIRE effect at approval is journal lines — `ApprovalService`'s Contra strategy is `postContra` and nothing else, and a Journal is `postJournalLines` and nothing else. A scenario takes an entry out of the general ledger and out of nothing else, so these are the two that can be left out of it.

⚠️ A payment or receipt SETTLES: `applyReceiptSettlement` moves `trx.paidAmount` and the register writes an `against` reference against a bill that IS in the books. Money out of the accounts cannot close an invoice in them. The sentence names the settlement rather than reciting the rule, and points at the Journal — a refusal whose message does not describe the actual problem is BUG-0015's own tell.

⚠️ The OTHER reason, and it needs its own sentence because a single message would be true of neither half. These move stock (`InventoryService.apply` reads no journal entry and has no scenario to consult) and are GST documents (`GstReturnAssemblyService` assembles GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B from `trx` rows by status, never from `journal_lines`) — so a "provisional" invoice would be declared to the government while being out of the accounts.

⚠️ An unrecognised kind is REFUSED, not waved through — the safe branch by default (BUG-0065's shape). `Journal` capitalised is here because the set is matched exactly: a case-insensitive match on one side and not the other is drift the sentence alone would not show.
